The sheet now has a grace-days setting, and changing the sheet's today closes any overdue open periods. All 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

**What changed:**
- **Setting:** `grace-days` is a new setting on the sheet. It takes a whole number of days, blank turns it off, and it isn't dated. Saving it writes `SETTING_CHANGED key=grace-days value=<days>`. The Settings panel has a new field (`setting-grace-days`) that shows the current value (`setting-grace-days-current`). As with the policy date, clearing a field that is already blank still saves the blank.
- **Shared close:** I moved the closing logic out of `ClosePeriod` into a new `PeriodCloser` service (`src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/period/PeriodCloser.java`). A close by hand and an automatic close now run the same code. The only difference is that an automatic close adds ` auto=yes` to the end of its `PERIOD_CLOSED` line.
- **Today change:** `SaveToday` sets the new today first. It then closes every open period whose to-date plus the grace days is before the new today, in order of their to-dates. The rollup lines come after that, so the audit file has the order the request asks for. The screen already re-reads everything on the sheet after a today change, so the closed periods show without any front-end change.

**Decision for you:** an automatic close skips the permission-matrix check for `close`. A close by hand still checks it, and the user changing the date only needs to be allowed to change today. "Exactly as a close by hand would" could also mean the automatic close should obey the matrix too. The tests don't settle it either way, so say if you want the check added.
